 Do vote 
 Date: October 19, 2026 
 My wife sent me a text – “I’ve just gone and voted.” In Virginia, you can do in-person voting for 45 days before Election Day. Election Day is Tuesday November 3, 2026. Looking ahead to that Tuesday, I find that my calendar is very full: Eucharist, then three meetings, search related events in the afternoon, and then an evening commitment with the Washington Theological Consortium. There will be very little space to cast my ballot, so I will be taking advantage of early voting.
 It is very tempting to imagine your vote does not matter, but of course, it’s this attitude that means that those who make the effort to vote find their votes matter even more. For every person who opts out, the person that actually exercises their democratic right has even more power. Elections are won by small margins: a few hundred here, a few thousand there. These margins are often determined by the individuals who, for whatever reason, found it too difficult to cast their vote that year.
 I do take the view that voting is a Christian obligation. It is a reminder that we do believe that the people who govern should do so with the consent of the people. Finding time to exercise your right, a hard-fought, difficult right, is an important obligation.
 The Very Rev. Ian S. Markham Ph.D.
 Dean and President of Virginia Theological Seminary and the President of The General Theological Seminary.
